name: Vadimkin/ukrainian-air-raid-sirens-dataset (Dataset of air raid sirens in the Ukraine-Russia war), incl. issues #3-#7
type: dataset (GitHub repo with a Telegram-parser that regenerates CSVs daily via GitHub Actions)
year: Created 2022-03-17; last repo push 2026-10-17 (volunteer files only); official_data_*.csv last commit 2026-09-08 03:44 UTC, last record started 2026-09-07 05:28:22 UTC (checked 2026-10-17)
authors: Vadym Klymenko (GitHub: Vadimkin), sole human maintainer (38 commits); github-actions[bot] (1628 'Add new data' commits); Copilot agent (3 commits, PR #5)
popularity: 88 GitHub stars, 5 forks (2026-10-17); widely reused in Ukrainian student/Kaggle alert-forecasting projects [uncertain]
peer_review_status: Not peer-reviewed; volunteer-maintained open dataset (MIT license). Accuracy is not validated against an official ground truth; maintainer himself pointed users to the official API for 'more reliable data' (issue #3).
target_type: Not applicable (dataset, not a model). Provides alert intervals (started_at, finished_at) from which either onset or state targets can be built; our project builds an ONSET target.
target_definition: Not applicable. Raw unit of record = one alert interval for one location (oblast, raion or hromada) with started_at/finished_at in UTC; no horizon.
spatial_unit: Mixed: oblast, raion and hromada rows (column `level`). After dedup: raion 99,304, oblast 65,314, hromada 20,812. Since Dec 2025 mostly raion-level (per datasets/README). Volunteer files are oblast-only.
at_risk_masking: Not applicable (dataset). Note for users: the dataset records only CLOSED alerts; alerts still open at each daily run are kept in a pickle (processors/pkl/official_active_alerts.pkl) and are not in the CSV, so 'currently under alert' cannot be read from the CSV at its end edge.
data_sources: Official file: parsed from the official Telegram channel t.me/air_alert_ua (Telethon client, OfficialAirAlertProcessor), records from 2022-03-15 16:10 UTC to 2026-09-07 05:28 UTC. Volunteer file: parsed from the eTryvoga Telegram channel, from 2022-02-25, oblast level only, still updating daily as of 2026-10-17. Permanent alerts in Luhansk (since 2022-04-04 16:45 UTC) and Crimea (since 2022-12-10 22:22 UTC) are NOT listed.
data_source_variant: Two variants: official_data_{en,uk}.csv (official channel; oblast+raion+hromada levels; columns oblast, raion, hromada, level, started_at, finished_at, source) and volunteer_data_{en,uk}.csv (eTryvoga; oblast only; has `naive` flag where finished_at = started_at + 30 min when no end message). English files are transliterations (translitua) of the Ukrainian ones; 'm. Kyiv' -> 'Kyiv City'. Snapshot used by our project: official_data_en.csv, 299,275 rows (frozen 2026-09-07).
preprocessing: Done by the dataset itself: none beyond parsing. Parser maps hashtags in the message's last line to (oblast, raion, hromada, level) via states.json + legacy_states renames + a hard-coded hromada_special_rules dict for duplicate hromada names; messages with any unknown hashtag or the 'Testovyi Region' are dropped entirely (logged, not raised). Appends to CSV in 'a' mode each daily run. Required on the user side (verified on our snapshot): exact-duplicate removal (113,845 of 299,275 rows, duplicates spread over all years 2022-2026), union of oblast/raion/hromada levels per oblast, gap masking 2026-08-30..09-01, standing-alert handling (897 alerts > 24h, 13 > 7 days after dedup), manual handling of Luhansk/Crimea permanent alerts.
known_label_artefacts: (1) EXACT DUPLICATES: 113,845/299,275 rows identical (38%), across all years; probable cause is append-mode writing combined with re-runs (workflow triggers on every push AND daily cron, state pickles committed) [uncertain cause]. Handling: drop_duplicates first (our CLAUDE.md rule). (2) SYNTHETIC 1-HOUR ENDS: in process_message, if a new 'alert' message arrives for a location whose previous alert has no 'all-clear' and >3 h have passed, the old alert is closed at started_at + 1 h (fabricated end). Our snapshot has 255 durations of exactly 3600 s to the second vs ~18 expected by chance from the 2,150 durations in 59-61 min, i.e. roughly 235 synthetic ends; rising over time (2022:10, 2023:17, 2024:32, 2025:48, 2026:148), concentrated in Dnipropetrovska (67) and Zaporizka (59). Not flagged in the data. (3) SILENT OVERWRITE / LOST ONSETS: if a new alert message arrives <3 h after an unclosed one, the earlier alert object is replaced and never written, so that onset disappears from the file. (4) DROPPED MESSAGES: a message with any hashtag missing from states.json is skipped in full (all its locations), losing starts or ends; a lost end then produces artefact (2) or (3). (5) SWAPPED COLUMNS (issue #4 / PR #5, fixed 2026-01-11): Hrebinkivska hromada rows had oblast and raion swapped because the special-rules tuple order was wrong in code; data line 18 and the code were corrected; maintainer said there was 'an error in implementation as well'. Our snapshot line 18 is correct (Poltavska oblast, Lubenskyi raion). A follow-up commit 2026-01-25 'Update script to not skip renamed hromadas' means some renamed-hromada alerts were previously skipped [uncertain extent]. (6) WRONG DURATIONS (issue #3, opened 2024-10-28, closed 2026-09-25 without a data fix): user reported the 25.10.2024 Ivano-Frankivsk alert duration looked wrong; our snapshot has that alert lasting 4 seconds; 453 deduped alerts last < 1 minute and 2 exactly 0 s. (7) 30-MIN ENDS: the naive +30 min end rule exists only in the VOLUNTEER processor (`naive=True`); the official file has 38 exactly-30-min durations after dedup (68 before), not produced by any official-code rule, so likely genuine coincidences or channel-side artefacts [uncertain]; kept as-is (D-010). (8) STANDING ALERTS: very long hromada alerts (e.g. 604 days in Kharkivska) remain in the file; handled by our causal 24 h cap (D-020). (9) RECORDING GAP: no rows 2026-08-30 -> 2026-09-01, partial 29 Aug / 2 Sep; handled as MISSING (D-013). (10) FREEZE 2026-09-07 05:28 UTC (issues #6 2026-09-21 and #7 2026-09-25, both open, no maintainer reply): the official file stopped while volunteer files continue. Issue #7 hypothesises the 6 Sep 2026 yellow/red alert reform (CabMin resolution No. 1092) changed the Telegram message format; the parser recognises starts only by 'Povitriana' or the red-circle emoji and ends by 'Vidbii' or the green-circle emoji, and drops unknown formats, consistent with that hypothesis [uncertain]. Alerts open at freeze time stay in the pickle and never reach the CSV, so the end edge is right-censored. (11) PERMANENT ALERTS Luhansk/Crimea not listed (README).
features: Not applicable (dataset). Raw fields usable for features: oblast, raion, hromada, level, started_at, finished_at (UTC). No threat type, no yellow/red level, no alert id, no update timestamp (unlike alerts.in.ua API).
external_feature_timing: Not applicable. Publication timing note: CSVs are committed once a day (~03:40 UTC) and only contain alerts already closed, so a live system using this file sees end times with up to ~24 h delay and never sees open alerts.
calibration_under_drift: Not applicable directly. Relevant drift in the data itself: the share of raion-level alerts rises sharply from Dec 2025 (admin reform), synthetic 1-h ends grow ~15x 2022->2026, and the file ends at the Sep-2026 yellow/red reform, so no post-reform official data exists in this source.
regime_coverage: Covers 2022-03-15 to 2026-09-07: includes the Jan-2025 drone surge period and the Dec-2025 raion-level reform, but ends at the 2026-09-06/07 yellow/red reform (no new-regime data). 7-12 Sep 2026 is missing from both this file and alerts.in.ua history.
leakage_handling: Not applicable (dataset). Leakage-relevant properties for users: (a) finished_at is the FINAL end time, only known after the fact; using it to classify alerts (e.g. 'standing') at forecast time leaks (our D-020 avoids this); (b) synthetic +1 h ends are written retroactively when the next alert arrives >3 h later, so the 'end' is a fabrication created with future information; (c) daily append + duplicates mean row order is not a reliable time index; (d) no per-row publication/ingestion timestamp exists, so a true as-of-t reconstruction of what the file contained at t is impossible; the closest causal proxy is started_at <= t and finished_at <= t.
test_window_hygiene: Not applicable (dataset). Note: the official file can still change retroactively (e.g. PR #5 rewrote line 18 in Jan 2026), so a test window must be pinned to a dated snapshot.
headline_results: Not applicable (dataset). Key verified numbers on our snapshot (2026-10-17 check): 299,275 rows; 113,845 exact duplicates; 185,430 unique rows; started_at range 2022-03-15 16:10:34 -> 2026-09-07 05:28:22 UTC; 897 alerts > 24 h; 255 exactly-1 h durations (mostly synthetic); 38 exactly-30 min; 453 < 1 min; 0 negative durations; 0 missing finished_at.
code_available: Yes. MIT license. Python 3.10 + Telethon parser (process.py, processors/), GitHub Actions daily cron 00:00 UTC + on push; requires Telegram API credentials to regenerate. Maintenance: official stream broken since 2026-09-07 with open issues #6/#7 unanswered as of 2026-10-17; volunteer stream active.
takeaways_for_project: 1. Keep 'dedup first and print the count' (CLAUDE.md data rule): duplicates are 38% of rows and spread across all years, so any count before dedup is wrong. 2. Add an explicit data-quality print/flag for exactly-3600 s durations: ~235 are fabricated by the parser's 3-hour rule; they distort minutes_since_last_end and the D-020 'active' state (a real alert lasting e.g. 5 h is truncated to 1 h). Consider a test that counts them and a note in the README; do NOT silently drop them (no silent fallbacks). Changing how they are handled is a rule change for Oleksandr. 3. Onsets are undercounted where the parser overwrote unclosed alerts (<3 h rule) or dropped messages with unknown hashtags; these losses are invisible in the CSV, so the onset base rate from this source is a lower bound; state this as a limitation in README. 4. The D-010 '30-min ends' concern comes from the VOLUNTEER naive rule; in the official file the analogous artefact is the 1-hour synthetic end, so D-010 wording should reference the right mechanism. 5. Issue #3 (4-second Ivano-Frankivsk alert) and 453 sub-minute alerts: sub-minute alerts still create onsets in our target; worth a printed count and a sensitivity check (onset rate with/without < 1 min alerts). 6. Freeze at 2026-09-07 05:28 confirms D-007/D-015: the official file cannot cover the yellow/red regime; the end edge is right-censored (open alerts never written), so the last hours before 2026-09-07 05:28 should be masked or the test end kept at 2026-09-07 00:00 as now. 7. Use the dataset's oblast column for the union (D-017), but pin the snapshot: the file was edited retroactively (PR #5) and our raw download should record its git commit SHA / download date in run_meta.json. 8. Never mix with volunteer_data_* (different channel and naive-end rule), confirmed by the code.
best_practices: Adopt: (a) treat community-parsed alert data as noisy: dedup, flag synthetic durations (exactly 3600 s, exactly 1800 s), flag sub-minute and > 24 h alerts, and print each count at load time; (b) record source snapshot provenance (repo commit SHA of datasets/official_data_en.csv, download date) because the file can be rewritten; (c) read the parser code before modelling: it reveals fabricated ends (+1 h after 3 h), dropped messages and right-censoring of open alerts that are not documented in the README; (d) treat the gap and the freeze as missing data, not zero alerts; (e) keep Luhansk excluded and Crimea absent. Anti-patterns: using raw row counts before dedup; computing durations or 'standing' status from final finished_at at forecast time; treating 1-h synthetic ends as real all-clears; assuming the CSV is a complete record of onsets; mixing official and volunteer files; using row order as time order; assuming the official stream continues past 2026-09-07.
